lead.headline: 193 providers on the federal health-fraud ban list took about $166K from drug companies in 2024
lead.number: 193 banned NPIs paid about $166K in 2024; one row is $114K (Hector Molina, TX, "debt forgiveness" from Skye Orthobiologics).
lead.watch_out: One row carries most of the dollars, and WAS_REINSTATED is False on every row, so that filter removes nothing.

sources.quote: Of 3,725 excluded clinicians identified, 16.2% (n=605) received one or more payments.
sources.page_context: ted the total, median, and interquartile range of dollar values per clinician and per payment, by category of payment. The study was determined to be not human subjects research by the Oregon Health & Science University Institutional Review Board because it involved publicly available data. RESULTS Of 3,725 excluded clinicians identified, 16.2% (n=605) received one or more payments. These clinicians were mostly physicians (83.3%) or dentists (12.2%) and mostly male (79.3%; Table 1 ). Of 621 available exclusion reasons, conviction of program-related crimes (34.6%) was the most common. There were 7,061 payments totaling $2,286,339 ( Table 2 ).
